lines.en: The morning arrives unceremoniously, and with it comes the inherent desire to fall back asleep and ignore the customary closing ceremony entirely.

I say this not only as someone who isn’t excited to hear the results, but as someone who has already experienced one timeskip during this exact event. And I’d much prefer to not have to do that again.
Also, you’ll probably be proud to hear that I went to bed normally and allowed Imani and Wakana to sleep through the night this time.
And yes, it wasn’t a comfortable night for me as I’m far more used to an actual bed than a futon, but at least they allowed me to stay outside of the closet rather than locking me in it.
Because, honestly, if they tried, I likely would have let them.
I did not end last night in a good place — but that will all change today.
Today, I will go back to normal and live my life as a normal guy who likes normal things and does normal stuff.
I am no longer a danger to society.
I am reformed and ready to live happily ever after.
But of course that all changes the moment I walk past Kirin and Noriko being lesbians on my way to meet up with everyone else.
I clearly still have a long way to go.
But I don’t need to rush as much as I have been.
My time here is endless after all.
And nothing will ever go wrong again.
: Noriko, have I ever told you how beautiful you are?
: Yes. Mostly while I’m getting dressed. And for what I imagine is the thousandth time now, thank you. I think you’re cute too.
: Cute? Or beautiful?

: Cute. But not, like...innocent-cute. The kind of cute where a little girl is crying in the grocery store because her mom won’t buy her ice cream and she tries to put on a strong face even though she really wants it.
: You know what? I’ll take it. Thanks.
: Any time. That’s what friends are for.
: Kirin...are you a lesbian?
: Oh, Karin. I must not have realized you were there on account of how uninteresting and forgettable you are.
: But we walked here together...
: Yeah, that’s why I added the “forgettable” part. Also, no. I like dicks too much to be a lesbian. Girls are hot too, though.
: I never knew that you felt that way. Thank you for opening up to me. And please know that I’ll support you no matter who you love.
: Blech.
: What do you think it would take to get her to really come after me? Like in an “I’m telling our parents sort of way.”
: Aww, there you go being cute again. Just instead of it being about ice cream, it’s about how you want your big sister to pay attention to you.
: Bite me.
: Sure. Getting frisky in public might get her to scold you for a little while. That’s what you want, right?
: No matter who you love.
: Nah, I’m pretty sure she’d just buy us a “congratulations” card if we did that.
: I’m so happy you’ve found such a good friend.
: God, you’re so annoying! Stop being so good and go get corrupted like the rest of us!
: Ignoring whatever the heck is going on over there, welcome to the closing ceremony for the third annual Super Mega Ultimate Dorm Wars!
: We’ve had a heck of a good time over the last couple days, haven’t we?
: Like...sure! Two of us got lost in the woods! And Miss Watabe almost called the cops on us. And Nodoka was weird again. And Yumi and Tsuneyo almost killed each other.
: And four of us didn’t really get to do anything on the second day. And Sensei has been all over the place. And Noriko killed Rin. And I had to touch a weird fish with a face. And-
: We get it, Uta. It wasn’t a perfect weekend by any means, but it was still fun. And I say that as one of the four who didn’t really get to do anything on the second day.
: We could just avoid this in the future by not combining our special events anymore, you know. With how exciting they are on their own, there’s really no need to cram two into one weekend.
: Well said, Miss Imai!
: Now, the moment you’ve all been waiting for! Or at least...the moment some of you have been waiting for as a bunch of you seem rather disinterested right now.
: Just recap the winners for ‘em, Makocchi. Anyone who isn’t paying attention can shove it.
: Right. Yes. Well, then...
: In regard to the horror story writing contest, the winner is...Futaba Fukuyama!
: Woo! Congrats to Futaba on beating a robot- she’s not paying attention, is she?
: It doesn’t look that way, no.
: What are you writing, Nodoka?
: Nothing, my dear. I’m simply looking over the notes I took yesterday.
: You were taking notes yesterday? On what?
: On the people and things I found interesting.
: I’m seeing...Ami’s name...all over the place in there...
: Yes. Because she is interesting.
: Well, I...I tried to tell you yesterday, but I wouldn’t mind asking her if the two of you could-
: There’s no need. I’ll handle it myself. But thank you.
: Oh. Uhh...okay. I suppose that’s fine too...
: Moving things right along, the next contest winner we’d like to announce is...
: Rin Rokuhara! Who defeated her arch nemesis, Molly MacCormack, in a heated battle of the chefs that no one saw coming!
: Dorm 4 sweep! Let’s fucking gooooooo!
: Makoto, careful. Your poor competitive spirit is showing again.
: Sorry. I’m just excited to start the competition up 2-0.
: Don’t get too excited, Makoto. We’ve still got eight other contests to read out.
: Hey, Otoha. You should give me a reward for winning my contest.
: Should I? Why’s that?
: Because I suck and never win at anything, but I somehow did this year. Which means we should celebrate because this may never happen again.
: Is there something in particular you had in mind?
: Maaaaaaaaybe?
: Is it something you can say out loud?
: Uuuuuuuuuuuhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh...
: You know what? Why don’t you just text it to me?
: Our next competition is one of two we conducted on our own yesterday while the rest of you were off having fun.
: And fortunately for the girls of the second floor, this one was won by our very own Io Ichimonji, who defeated Miku Maruyama in a quest to build a raft!
: This brings the initial score of the Dorm Wars up to 2-1 with the first floor still one point ahead!
: Sorry for lettin’ ya down, Sana. I’d like to say I tried my hardest, but I know that ain’t the case. Really dropped the ball on this one. Just the ball is a plank of wood or somethin’.
: Y...You don’t have to...apologize to me...I...I never really expected you to...win in the...first place...
: Well thanks for all the faith ya have in me.
: It’s just...Io is...she...likes to build things...doesn’t she?
: Yeah, and she’s like...crazy good at it too! You should’a seen the raft thingy she put together. It managed to carry all four of us.
: How’d your contest go, by the way? You manage to get a good confession out?
: I...actually don’t know yet...
: I left before...Otoha had her turn and...I haven’t really talked to Sensei ever since...
: Think you’ve got a shot? A win now would put us up three to one. And it ain’t like Otoha and Sensei are really “couple” material, ya know?
: Are you saying...Sensei and I...are?...
: Sure. If ya don’t mind gettin’ split in half.
: If I...don’t mind getting-
: IN REGARD TO THE CONFESSION BATTLE!
: Wait! Here we go! The moment of truth!
: The winner of the first installment in what we hope will be a brand new contest series is...
: The only girl around who’s smaller than yours truly...Sana Sakakibara!

: Ayyyyy! Atta girl! Better kiss those lady parts goodbye, though. Sensei’s probably gonna tear ya to shreds if that confession was good enough to have him pick you over one of the coolest girls in school.
: I...won? He picked me?
: Sure sounds that way. You excited? How do ya feel pickin’ up a win after Molly took ya down last year?
: I feel...really good...actually...
: After...Sensei’s reaction yesterday...I wasn’t sure if...if he really...um...
: Well, seemed like whatever you were worryin’ about didn’t matter at all. Either that or Otoha’s confession just really stunk. But hey, what ya don’t know can’t hurt ya.
: Someone way too cool for school...and another member of the second floor, Otoha Okakura!
: Tch. And there goes our lead, just like that.
: Hah...I had a...feeling this would happen...
: My...um...strategy wasn’t as...effective as...I thought it would be...
: Well, what was the strategy? Gettin’ to Sensei’s heart ain’t as hard as ya might think. He’s a boy through and through.
: That’s...kind of what I...
: Actually, never mind. I don’t...really want to talk about it...
: Tch. Friggin’ Otoha bein’ all cool and stuff. Here’s hopin’ whoever comes next is able to get us back on track.
: As many of you may know, I came up with a brand new challenge this year.
: And everyone hated it!
: Yes. Thank you, Uta. Everyone hated it. But that does not mean the points do not count...despite how much I may want them not to count as the second floor somehow managed to win.
: So congratulations to Tsuneyo and Noriko who have earned two more points for the second floor.
: Mwahahaha! We have them right where we want them, Kendo Princess!
: You didn’t even do anything.
: Sometimes, when your inclusion will only make the fight harder, it is best to stand off to the side and let your party carry you so you do not ruin things for everyone else.
: Today is one of those days. And the next round at the tavern will be on my tab as my means of saying thanks.
: I do not need a “round at the tavern.” I need you to pay as much attention to me as I pay attention to you. That is the way a friendship should function, and you have disappointed me greatly.
: You’re still upset about that?
: I’m furious, bro.
: I meant no disrespect! I just know what I am and am not capable of!
: Hi. Io here. You can go back to ignoring me forever once I’m done talking. In fact, please do exactly that.
: But anyway, somebody told me the other day that expecting to fail at something is a problem in and of itself.
: She said that anyone is capable of anything so long as they try their hardest. So there’s no challenge ever worth backing away from.
: Was she faced with such a challenge? Did she overcome the odds and emerge victorious despite what she and everyone else likely believed?
: No. She was wrong and she gave up. So I think the Irish girl isn’t wrong in not following through with something she knows she would suck at. Wasting your energy is stupid.
: Ha!
: You are all extremely disappointing.
: Our next contest, and arguably the most controversial based on whether or not you think it’s okay for teenage girls to strip for their teacher-
: It’s not. Just so everyone knows, it’s definitely not.
: ...is the one where we sent two girls out into the woods without a GPS and expected them to get back within a reasonable amount of time! Boy were we wrong!
: But despite that, one girl did come out on top. And that girl was the one with more experience getting lost than anyone...Yasu Yasui.
: Who is also not paying attention.
: Does she ever?
: You okay, Touka? Still upset about Yasu’s contest?
: How could I not be when the lot of you decided it was acceptable to put poor Yasu in danger?
: Hey, don’t lump me in with them. I think this whole ass contest is stupid as shit.
: And yet you participated this year. Curious.
: I only fuckin’ did that because I knew you’d throw a hissy fit if I didn’t.
: Sure. I can believe that. But I’d much rather believe that you’re finally coming around to accept just how great Sensei is and that you’ve been wrong about him this whole time. Right, Touka?

: While I admit that my initial judgment of him may have been a bit harsh, I am not quite sure if I would preach about his greatness just yet. He still has a long way to come in regard to being a respectable adult.
: Tsk, tsk, tsk. None of you get it. But that’s fine. I’m the oldest and most mature after all. And if anyone knows best, it’s me.
: Yeah, not sure about that one, Chika. Think Princess Tits over here might have you beat in the maturity department.
: Princess...Tits?
: Oh, so you can comment on Touka’s boobs but not mine? Real cool, Yumi. Real cool.
: What is with your weird obsession with getting me to talk about your tits lately?!
: It’s only fair that you pay attention to my chest when I look at yours all the time.
: Stop! That’s literally sexual harassment!
: And...calling me “Princess Tits” is not?
: Our next competition is the other most controversial one we held this year.
: Which, once again, depends entirely on whether or not you think it’s okay for teenage girls to strip for their teacher.
: Which, once again, it’s not.
: And the winner of this competition is...Uta Ushibori!
: But don’t ask me how or why because I 100%% would have picked Chika instead!
: Great. Now I have to remember that I lost the swimsuit competition on top of my best friend reminding me she hates my boobs.
: Wonder if that’s why Shortstack won. Maybe it really was just a tits competition at the end of the day?
: That’s what I keep telling myself and it doesn’t make this any easier.
: For what it’s worth, I think both of you are quite beautiful. And I’m sure it’s only a matter of personal preference.
: Yeah. And if it ain’t a tits thing, we can just assume our weirdo teacher picked the tiny one since she looks more like a kid than you do.
: Thank you, Yumi. I love you. Next year, you can defend my honor by competing in the boobs competition in my place.
: Yeah, that ain’t happenin’.

: And the winner of this competition is Chika Chosokabe because of course it is! Congratulations, Chika! You’re beautiful and sexy and I can’t wait to see you in a maid outfit and I’m going to shut up now!
: Thank you, Uta! You were great too! And you can see me in anything you want whenever you want.
: Well, that’s a fucking gross thing to say.
: You just don’t get it, Yumi. Girls have to say that kind of stuff to one another so we can build each other up since the world is always trying to drag us down.
: The compliments, I get. That shit’s fair. But the “You can see me in anything you want, whenever you want” bullshit? The fuck is up with that?
: Oh, I just like making Uta blush and I’m pretty sure she has a thing for me.
: And this is probably why Headphones was obsessed with you for a hundred years.
: Rin hasn’t worn headphones since we first started high school. Also, I didn’t flirt with her on purpose and she was way more awkward than Uta is.
: Also, neither one of you has congratulated me yet and I’m still waiting for it.
: Congratulations, Chika. You broke several laws very effectively and have set an example for all of us.
: Thank you, Touka. Now, Yumi. Your turn.
: Congrats on...giving a predator a boner?
: Thank you as well.
: Oh, also, I won the fishing competition in case anyone was wondering. Which no one probably is since Kirin is all the way over there and no one cares about fishing.
: Woo! Go Makoto!
: But that brings us to the announcement of our final competition’s winner! Which was both expected and somehow unexpected as she received a major handicap thanks to a guest judge!
: What is this? Why is she just clinging to him and why is no one saying anything about it?
: Because it’s Ayane and that’s what she does.
: Yes, but she is supposed to do it in a way that is both less public and less abrasive.
: There’s nothing abrasive about this, Ami! And I’m totally fine with you taking the other arm if it gets you to stop whining!
: Is that not abrasive? That had to be abrasive, right? Am I using that word correctly?
: Is everything okay with you? You seem...different. At least from how you’ve been lately.
: I just want to know why no one is doing anything about this. That is all.
: Is everything okay, Ayane? You’ve been...really clingy since I got here.
: I know! And Ami hasn’t done anything about it! It’s like magic, right?
: That’s not how I’d describe it, no. But, so long as no one else sees a problem with it, I don’t really mind.
: Good! Cause I’ll be clinging to you a lot more from this point on and there’s nothing you or anyone else can do about it.
: Hey, are you guys done talking over there yet? Because we kind of need to announce that Ami defeated Touka in order to start wrapping things up.
: And I think you kind of just did.
: Congratulations, Ami! I’m sure you won fair and square and didn’t use any sort of nefarious tactics whatsoever!
: I don’t even know how I won that competition! Or what “nefarious” even means!
: Yeah, that tracks.
: Ayane, can you maybe get your hands-
: Nope! I’m here to stay and that’s a thing you’re just going to have to learn how to deal with!
: So! Now that all of the winners have been announced, it’s time for the final tally!

: However! There is still the matter of distributing the bonus points from last year’s Dorm Wars winner in lieu of an actual prize! Which may very well tip the scales of this war in the opposite direction!
: And since that winner was the first floor, we’ll be adding two more points to their total for this year’s competition! Don’t all scream at once!
: That being said-
: And since the gals of the second floor got that win last year, we’ll be adding two more points to our total for this year’s competition! Heck yeah!
: That being said-
: The final score...
: For this year’s Dorm Wars...
: Is [beachwarfloor1points] to [beachwarfloor2points] in favor of the first floor! We did it, girls!
: Congratulations, Makoto. And all of the people not named Makoto who also care this much.
: And congratulations to my girls for doing your best...we’ll get ‘em next year.
: So, now that we’re done here...what now? Are we still going to school today?
: Oh, crap! I completely forgot it was Monday!
: Is [beachwarfloor2points] to [beachwarfloor1points] with the second floor coming out on top! We did it, y’all!
: And we, regretfully...did not. But I suppose there’s always next year.
: And I suppose I’ll start freeing up my schedule for the sleepover so all of you don’t stay at Senpai’s house unchaperoned!
: So, now that we’re done here...what now? Are we still going to school today?
: Oh, crap! I completely forgot it was Monday!
: Is [beachwarfloor1points] to [beachwarfloor2points].
: We apparently tied.
: What does this mean for the sleepover thing, then? Are...Are all twenty of you going to his house?
: Sensei, permission to be suffocating for a second?
: Permission granted. That’s too many people.
: None of you are coming over! The end!
: What are we doing? We once again failed to think up a system that would both prevent this from happening or decide what we’re supposed to do in the event of a stalemate.
: There’s always a coin flip.
: Yeah, but that’s boring.
: Sure, but the alternative is the two of us ultimately forgetting that we tied this year until we’re distributing the contests for the next Dorm Wars.
: Well, I don’t know about you, but I’m fine with future Uta handling this problem.
: Yeah, we’ve been here long enough and we still have to go to school today.
: Oh, crap! I completely forgot it was Monday!
: Everybody who’s not already packed, get your shit or we’re all going to get in trouble!
: Noriko and I are gonna stay here for the rest of the day! But the rest of you can go have fun!
: I would also like to stay-
: Oh, no! You’re coming with me!
Imani grabs my arm and starts dragging me toward the bus stop. Which means that, by extension, she grabs Ayane as well.
Which, of course, means that Ami has to follow after us. Then Maya.
Then everyone else.
Except Kirin and Noriko, of course. But I suppose we’ll see them again tomorrow.
Either way, we managed to make it through yet another installment of the Dorm Wars.
And once again, I managed to stay sane.
Mostly.
Partially.
Not really.
My brain feels like it’s full of worms.
But that’s okay.
Because nothing will ever go wrong again.
Nothing will ever go wrong again.
Nothing will ever go wrong again.
The end.
